remark.usage: 族：remarkable a. 卓越的；非凡的；近义：comment n. 意见，评论；[族] remarkable adj. 非凡的；值得注意的；辨析:comment批评解释说明;commentary对文章作品解释评语,实况解说;remark口头或书面随意发表的意见；索引p415

ex.en: His careless remark offended several members of the audience.
ex.zh: 他随口的一句话冒犯了几位听众。

ex.en: In her opening remarks, the minister thanked the volunteers.
ex.zh: 部长在开场白中向志愿者们表示感谢。

ex.en: Critics remarked that the novel lacked originality.
ex.zh: 评论家们评论说这部小说缺乏新意。

senses: adj. 显著的；值得注意的
adj. 值得注意的,非凡的,卓越的
adj. 显著的，值得注意的；卓越的

phrases.m: 以...而著称,因...而引人注意

remarkable.usage: remark 的派生词；[族] remarkably adv. 显著地；引人注目地；助记:remark(引人注目)+able(形容词后缀)→非凡的；adj.引人注目的，非凡的；词根记忆：remark(评论)+able(可…的)→可圈可点的→非凡的；索引p415

ex.en: Remarkable changes have taken place in the book business.
ex.zh: 图书业发生了显著的变化。

ex.en: She made remarkable progress in a single term, moving from the bottom of the class to the top ten.
ex.zh: 她在一个学期内取得了显著的进步，从班里的最后几名跃升进入前十名。

ex.en: The desert plant has a remarkable ability to survive for months without any rainfall.
ex.zh: 这种沙漠植物具有惊人的能力，可以在无雨的条件下存活数月。

senses: adv. 显著地；引人注目地
remarkably.usage: adv.不寻常地，惊人地 中国城市化arose,速度之快让所有人shock。我们有幸成为了witnesses,quote 一个拥有很大reputation 的经济学家的话，rural 人口的城市化会让在校的undergraduatessus

ex.en: The two reports are remarkably similar.
ex.zh: 这两份报告非常相似。

ex.en: The patient recovered remarkably quickly after the operation.
ex.zh: 病人术后恢复得非常快。

ex.en: Children raised in different countries show remarkably similar patterns of language development.
ex.zh: 在不同国家长大的儿童表现出极为相似的语言发展模式。

remedy.usage: re（回）+medy（药）→用药把身体调回来→疗法；索引p415

ex.en: This situation is easily remedied.
ex.zh: 这种情形易于补救。

ex.en: By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace.
ex.zh: 某个问题待其得到解决和补救时，它可能已经在市场上消失了。

ex.en: There is no simple remedy for the shortage of affordable housing.
ex.zh: 对于保障性住房短缺问题，没有简单的补救办法。

senses: vt. 使想起；使记起；提醒
remind.usage: [族] reminder n. 提示；提醒物；同义: prompt, suggest to；索引p415

ex.en: Britain's new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance, not just for the short term but for the long term.
ex.zh: 英国的新规定提醒银行家,社会不仅对他们的短期业绩有兴趣,而且对他们的长期业绩也有兴趣。

ex.en: Please remind me to call the bank before it closes at four.
ex.zh: 请提醒我在银行四点关门之前打电话。

ex.en: The smell of hay always reminds her of summers on her grandfather's farm.
ex.zh: 干草的气味总让她想起在祖父农场度过的夏天。

ex.en: The cracked window was a constant reminder of the storm.
ex.zh: 那扇破裂的窗户时刻提醒着人们那场暴风雨。

ex.en: The app sends a daily reminder so that users do not miss their medication.
ex.zh: 这款应用每天发送提醒，以免用户忘记服药。

ex.en: The report serves as a reminder that economic growth alone does not guarantee happiness.
ex.zh: 该报告提醒人们，仅靠经济增长并不能保证幸福。

senses: n. (pl.)残余,剩余;遗迹,遗风;幸存者
vt. 改变…的形状（或结构）
adj. 持续恶化的;无休止的;残酷的
adj. 无情的;无同情心的

remote.usage: [族] remotely adv. 遥远地；略微；re（回）+mote（动）→移到很远的地方→遥远的；同义: distant；adj.边远的；遥远的；久远的； 远程的 n.遥控器；re（向后，重复）+mot（=move）+e→往后移动越来越远→遥远的。；真 remote villages 偏远乡村；索引p415

ex.en: The area is remote, mountainous, and roadless.
ex.zh: 这个地区偏远、多山、没有道路。

ex.en: Is there any chance that Cardus's criticism will enjoy a revival? The prospect seems remote.
ex.zh: 卡达斯的艺术评论是否还会重新流行起来呢？希望似乎十分渺茫。

ex.en: Children in remote villages once walked hours to school, but online classes have changed that.
ex.zh: 偏远村庄的孩子们曾经要步行数小时去上学，而在线课程改变了这一状况。

removal.usage: [族] remove vt. 移开；去除（链接P218）；索引p415

ex.en: The removal of the old bridge took nearly three months.
ex.zh: 拆除旧桥花了将近三个月。

ex.en: The board voted for the immediate removal of the chief executive.
ex.zh: 董事会投票决定立即撤换首席执行官。

ex.en: The firm offers furniture removal services at competitive prices.
ex.zh: 这家公司以有竞争力的价格提供家具搬运服务。

remove.usage: eliminate 的近义词；同义: dismissal；vt.移开；除去，废除；把…… 免职，开除；脱下 n.距离，间距；re（反复，再一次）+move（移动）→再次移动，移走→移开。；remove 强调移走/去除具体或抽象的事物；removal n. 移动，去除。；索引p415

ex.en: The shortage is compounded by federal immigration raids, which remove some workers and drive others underground.
ex.zh: 联邦政府对移民的突击检查加剧了劳动力短缺，因为这些突击检查赶走了一些工人，另一些人则被迫转入地下工作。

ex.en: The old building was removed last year.
ex.zh: 那座旧建筑去年被拆除了。

senses: n. 文艺复兴,文艺复兴时期
n. 任何类似的复兴,再生
n. (the R-) 文艺复兴(时期)；复兴
renaissance.usage: 助记:re(again再)+naiss(出生)+ance(名词后缀)→重获新生→文艺复兴；索引p415

ex.en: The Renaissance produced artists such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo.
ex.zh: 文艺复兴时期产生了列奥纳多·达·芬奇和米开朗基罗等艺术家。

ex.en: The city centre is enjoying a renaissance as young families move back downtown.
ex.zh: 随着年轻家庭迁回市中心，市中心正在复兴。

ex.en: There has been a renaissance of interest in traditional crafts in recent years.
ex.zh: 近年来，人们对传统手工艺的兴趣再度复兴。

senses: vt. 使成为；使处于某状态
vt. 使变得；使处于某状态
render.usage: [族] rendering n. 演奏；表演；本身为词根，意为“翻译”。近义：offer vt. 提供。；近义：make 使得；provide 提供；[近] provide vt. 提供；熟词生义：render 本义“给予”，此处引申为“使成为”；[链 P289 render sth. into... 把……翻译成……

ex.en: Yet as we report now, the food police are determined that this enjoyment should be rendered yet another guilty pleasure guaranteed to damage our health.
ex.zh: 正如我们现在报告的那样,食品警察坚持认为,这一享受应被视为又一种罪恶的快乐,而这种快乐肯定会损害我们的健康。

ex.en: Suffering is inevitable, but the courage to fight it renders life worth living.
ex.zh: 痛苦是不可避免的，但与之抗争的勇气正是生活的意义所在。

ex.en: One could interpret much of the work of Beethoven by saying that suffering is inevitable, but the courage to fight it renders life worth living.
ex.zh: 人们可以这样来解释贝多芬的许多作品：痛苦是不可避免的，但正是和痛苦搏斗的勇气才使得生命富有意义。

senses: v. 违背(诺言);背信弃义;食言
vt. 重新开始；延长……的期限；重申；更新
renew.usage: [族] renewal n. 更新；续期；[族] renewable adj. 可再生的；同义:regain,refresh;reinforce;resume;派生renewable可再生的；真 renew their wardrobe 更新他们的衣橱；索引p415

ex.en: These labels encourage style-conscious consumers to see clothes as disposable and to renew their wardrobe every few weeks.
ex.zh: 这些品牌鼓励那些有时尚意识的消费者把衣服看作一次性的消费品，并且鼓动他们每几周就更新他们的衣柜。

ex.en: I need to renew my passport before travelling abroad.
ex.zh: 出国旅行前我需要换发护照。

ex.en: The two sides agreed to renew their trade agreement for five years.
ex.zh: 双方同意将贸易协定续签五年。

senses: adj. 可再生的；可续期的
adj. 可再生的；可更新的
renewable.usage: 真 renewable sources 可再生能源；索引p415

renewal.usage: 真 urban renovation and renewal 市区的整修和重建；索引p415

senses: v. 修复，翻新；重新粉刷
renovate.usage: 派生renovation修复,整修;革新,更新；v.修复，翻新；re(再)+nov(=new“新的”)+ate(动词后缀)→再次使它变成“新的”→翻新；索引p415

ex.en: The couple spent a year renovating the old farmhouse.
ex.zh: 这对夫妇花了一年时间翻修那座旧农舍。

ex.en: The city has renovated dozens of historic buildings in the old quarter.
ex.zh: 该市已翻新了老城区数十座历史建筑。

ex.en: Renovating the stadium is expected to cost more than fifty million dollars.
ex.zh: 翻修体育场预计耗资超过五千万美元。

renovation.usage: n.翻新，整修；n.修复，改造；翻新；索引p415

ex.en: The old theatre will reopen next year after a multi-million-pound renovation.
ex.zh: 经过数百万英镑的整修，这座老剧院将于明年重新开放。

ex.en: They bought the farmhouse cheaply and carried out most of the renovation themselves.
ex.zh: 他们低价买下农舍，大部分整修工程都是自己完成的。

ex.en: The renovation of the metro system has reduced overcrowding at rush hours.
ex.zh: 地铁系统的翻新缓解了高峰时段的拥挤。

senses: adj. 有名的;著名的;受尊敬的

rent.usage: [族] rental n. 租赁；租金；辨析:租房用rent,租设备用hire;rent from租入;rent to租出

ex.en: I can't afford to pay my monthly mortgage payments on my own, so I have to rent rooms out to people to make that happen.
ex.zh: 凭我一己之力无法负担月供，因此我不得不把房间出租给别人以负担月供。

ex.en: Rents in the capital have risen far faster than wages over the past decade.
ex.zh: 过去十年，首都的房租涨幅远远超过工资。

ex.en: They rent a small flat near the university and share the bills.
ex.zh: 他们在大学附近租了一套小公寓并分摊账单。

repair.usage: [近] fix vt. 修理；[近] mend vt. 修补

senses: v. 偿还，归还；报答，回报
repay.usage: [族] repayment n. 偿还；还款；re（表示“回来”）+pay（支付，付款）→归还；回报。

ex.en: Then, he can choose to turn to the bank for a loan to pay his way through university, which he can repay after graduation.
ex.zh: 然后，他可以选择向银行贷款，以支付大学学费，并在毕业后偿还。

ex.en: It took them ten years to repay the money they had borrowed.
ex.zh: 他们花了十年才还清所借的钱。

ex.en: She repaid his kindness by looking after him in his old age.
ex.zh: 他年迈时她悉心照料，以此报答他的恩情。

senses: vt. 重复；重说；重写；转述
repeat.usage: [族] repetition n. 重复；[族] repeatedly adv. 反复地

repeatedly.usage: 助记:repeated(重复的)+ly(副词后缀)→重复地

repel.usage: 助记:re(回)+pel(推)→击退;同义resist,reject;反义attract；v.击退，驱逐；抵御，驱除； 使反感；排斥，相斥；索引p415

ex.en: The fortress was designed to repel any attack from the north.
ex.zh: 这座堡垒的设计目的是击退来自北方的任何进攻。

ex.en: The smell of the plant repels many common insects.
ex.zh: 这种植物的气味能驱除许多常见昆虫。

ex.en: The coating repels water and keeps the shoes dry.
ex.zh: 这种涂层能排斥水分，使鞋保持干燥。

senses: n. [C-常用pl.] (间接的)影响，反响，恶果
n. (准备好演出的)节目,保留剧目
n. (美)(某个人的)全部技能;所有组成部分
n. 全部剧目；常备节目

replace.usage: [族] replacement n. 更换；替代者；[近] substitute vt. 代替；索引p415

ex.en: American manufacturing still needs to replace tens of thousands of retiring boomers every year.
ex.zh: 美国制造业每年仍需要替换数以万计的即将退休的婴儿潮一代人。

ex.en: By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power.
ex.zh: 当一个问题（用竞争法）处理和纠正完成时，这个问题可能已经在市场上消失，被新形式的权力滥用给替代了。

ex.en: Machines can replace repetitive manual labour, yet they seldom match human judgement in complex situations.
ex.zh: 机器可以取代重复性的体力劳动，但在复杂情境中却很少能与人类的判断力相匹敌。

senses: a. 可替代的；可被取代的
adj. 可替换的,可代替的

ex.en: All the parts of the machine are cheap and easily replaceable.
ex.zh: 这台机器的所有部件都很便宜，而且容易更换。

ex.en: The manager treats staff as replaceable parts rather than individuals.
ex.zh: 这位经理把员工当作可替换的零件而非独立的个人。

ex.en: Critics warn that in the gig economy workers are increasingly seen as replaceable.
ex.zh: 批评者警告说，在零工经济中，工人越来越被视为可以随意替换的。

senses: n. 更换，替换；替代的人或物
n. （尤指工作中的）代替者；替代品；替换
replacement.usage: n.代替，更换；取代的人(或物)；索引p415

ex.en: We must find a replacement for the retiring accountant.
ex.zh: 我们必须为即将退休的会计找一位接替者。

ex.en: The replacement of coal with cleaner fuels is gathering pace.
ex.zh: 用更清洁的燃料替代煤炭正在加速推进。

ex.en: The hotel ordered replacement windows after the storm.
ex.zh: 风暴过后，酒店订购了更换用的窗户。

report.usage: [族] reporter n. 记者；报道者；索引p415

ex.en: Yet as we report now, the food police are determined that this enjoyment should be rendered yet another guilty pleasure guaranteed to damage our health.
ex.zh: 然而正如我们现在所报告的，食品健康专家确信这种（周日烤肉带来的）愉悦极可能转化为另一种必将损害我们身体健康的负罪感。

ex.en: The committee will report its findings to Parliament next month.
ex.zh: 委员会将于下个月向议会报告调查结果。

ex.en: According to the report, one in four children leaves primary school unable to swim.
ex.zh: 报告显示，四分之一的儿童小学毕业时还不会游泳。

senses: n. 报告人,通讯员,记者,报导者
adj. 新闻报道的;记者的;记者工作的

represent.usage: [族] representative n. 代表；adj. 典型的（链接P220）；同义:symbolize;express,describe;stand for;派生representation代表,代理;表述；v.代表；表示；体现；描绘；re(阿姨)+present(出席)→会议我生病了，阿姨作为“代表”替我出席；

ex.en: In many cultures, the colour white represents purity, which explains its popularity at weddings.
ex.zh: 在许多文化中，白色象征纯洁，这解释了它在婚礼上受欢迎的原因。

ex.en: The survey sample was carefully chosen to represent voters of every age group and income level.
ex.zh: 调查样本经过精心挑选，以代表各个年龄段和收入水平的选民。

ex.en: Lawyers were hired to represent the workers in their dispute with the factory over unpaid wages.
ex.zh: 工人们聘请律师，在与工厂就拖欠工资问题产生的纠纷中代表他们。

senses: a. 具象派的；代表性的
adj. 具象派的;代表性的

ex.en: Abstract art abandoned representational painting in favour of colour and form.
ex.zh: 抽象艺术抛弃了具象绘画，转而追求色彩与形式。

ex.en: The gallery's earliest works are largely representational, showing recognisable people and places.
ex.zh: 该美术馆最早的作品大多是具象的，描绘可辨认的人物和地点。

ex.en: Critics debated whether the new sculpture was representational or purely abstract.
ex.zh: 评论家们争论这件新雕塑是具象的还是纯抽象的。

senses: adj. 典型的；有代表性的
representative.usage: 助记:represent(代表)+ative(形容词兼名词后缀)→代表；adj.典型的，有代表性的 n.代表；众议院议员；③ adj. 有代表性的（2010年阅读）；索引p415

ex.en: The ruling reinforces the need for citizens and their elected representatives.
ex.zh: 该裁决强化了公民和他们选出的代表的需要。

ex.en: In the landmark 1975 decision Taylor v. Louisiana, the Supreme Court extended the requirement that juries be representative of all parts of the community to the state level.
ex.zh: 在1975年这次具有里程碑意义的泰勒控告路易斯安那州的裁决中，最高法院将陪审团必须代表社区各个领域的规定延伸到了州一级。

ex.en: The union sent a representative to negotiate directly with management over the new pay scale.
ex.zh: 工会派出一名代表，就新的工资标准直接与管理层谈判。

ex.en: It's good to let your emotions show. Don't repress them.
ex.zh: 让你的情绪表现出来很好。不要压抑它们。

repression.usage: 助记:repress(镇压)+ion(名词后缀)→镇压;同根词repress压抑;repressive抑制的

senses: n. 责备,指责,斥责,批评
vt. 责备,指责,斥责,批评
reproach.usage: 助记:他的approach(态度)生硬,因此受到了reproach(指责)

reproduce.usage: [族] reproduction n. 复制；繁殖；[族] reproductive adj. 生殖的；re（再）+produce（生产）→再生产→复制；助记:re(again再)+produce(生产)→再次生产→繁殖

ex.en: Most reptiles reproduce by laying eggs on land.
ex.zh: 大多数爬行动物通过在陆地产卵进行繁殖。

ex.en: The report's findings could not be reproduced by independent researchers.
ex.zh: 独立研究人员无法重现该报告的结果。

ex.en: It is illegal to reproduce these images without the artist's permission.
ex.zh: 未经艺术家许可复制这些图片是违法的。

senses: adj. 可复制的；可再生的；可繁殖的
adj. 生殖的;再生的;再现的
reproductive.usage: adj.生殖的，繁殖的；翻印的， 复制的；索引p415

ex.en: The pesticide may harm the reproductive health of farm workers.
ex.zh: 这种杀虫剂可能损害农场工人的生殖健康。

ex.en: The study examined the reproductive behaviour of rare birds.
ex.zh: 这项研究考察了珍稀鸟类的繁殖行为。

ex.en: Better education tends to lower the reproductive rate of the population.
ex.zh: 更好的教育往往会降低人口的生育率。

republic.usage: 助记:re(前缀)+public(公共的,公开的)→共和国；索引p415

senses: adj. [R-]（美国）共和党的；共和国的
n. 共和党党员；共和主义者
republican.usage: 助记:republic(共和)+an(形容词后缀)→共和的；索引p415

ex.en: Charles ought to know that as English history shows, it is kings, not republicans, who are the monarchy's worst enemies.
ex.zh: 查尔斯应当知道，如同英国历史所表明的那样，君主制最大的敌人是国王，而不是共和党人。

reputation.usage: [族] repute n. 名声（链接P220）；辨析:reputation指大家公认的名声或特色;fame多指享有盛名且声望持续时间较长;honor指因人格或成就而受到他人崇敬；n.名誉，名声；re（重复，反复）+put（放）+ation（名词后缀）→他们重复地要求把你的名字放到前面，说明你的"名声"很大→名声；索引

ex.en: The company enjoys an international reputation for quality of design.
ex.zh: 该公司在设计质量方面享有国际声誉。

ex.en: A single food-safety scandal can destroy a reputation that took a company decades to build.
ex.zh: 一起食品安全丑闻就可能毁掉一家公司耗费数十年建立起来的声誉。

ex.en: The university's reputation rests largely on research output rather than on the quality of its teaching.
ex.zh: 这所大学的声誉主要建立在科研成果而非教学质量之上。

request.usage: [近] demand vt. 要求（语气更强）；n./v.要求，请求

ex.en: Visitors are requested not to touch the exhibits.
ex.zh: 请参观者不要触摸展品。

ex.en: She made a formal request for access to the documents.
ex.zh: 她正式提出查阅这些文件的请求。

ex.en: At the request of local residents, the council delayed the road works.
ex.zh: 应当地居民的要求，市政会推迟了道路施工。

senses: v. 需要；依靠；依赖；要求
require.usage: [族] requirement n. 要求；必要条件（链接P220）；v.需要；要求，规定；re（表示“重复”）+quire（=ask，问）→重复地问，为什么你重复地问一件事情呢？说明你需要这个信息→需要；要求；词根：re(表加强)+quir(ask询问)+e→不断询问是否做到→要求；索引p415

ex.en: If you require further information, you should consult the travel agency.
ex.zh: 如果需要进一步了解信息，请咨询旅行社。

ex.en: Nowadays anyone applying for a research post has to have published twice the number of papers that would have been required for the same post only 10 years ago.
ex.zh: 如今任何申请科研职位的人都必须已发表了论文，且数量是仅仅十年前申请同一职位所需论文数量的两倍。

ex.en: Learning a language to an advanced level requires sustained practice rather than occasional bursts of effort.
ex.zh: 把一门语言学到高级水平需要持续的练习，而不是偶尔的突击努力。

senses: n. 要求,需要;需要的东西
n. 需要的东西；必要条件
n. 要求（或必要条件）；所需的（或所要的）东西
requirement.usage: 辨析:requirement侧重于须满足的要求;requisite侧重于具体的必需物品；n.需求、要求；require 的派生词；索引p415

ex.en: What is the minimum entry requirement for this course?
ex.zh: 这门课程的最低入学要求是什么？

ex.en: Physical fitness is a basic requirement for firefighters, whose work demands strength and endurance.
ex.zh: 体能是消防员的基本要求，因为他们的工作需要力量和耐力。

ex.en: The scholarship has one strict requirement: recipients must return home and work for at least three years.
ex.zh: 这项奖学金有一项严格的要求：获得者必须回国工作至少三年。

senses: n. & v. 营救，救援；抢救
rescue.usage: [近] save vt. 救；re(再次,往回)+scue(音似secure安全的)→再次回到安全状态→救援

ex.en: Scientists jumped to the rescue with some distinctly shaky evidence.
ex.zh: 科学家们立即伸出援手，提出了一些明显站不住脚的证据。

ex.en: The fire crew rescued two children from the burning building.
ex.zh: 消防队员从燃烧的大楼里救出两名儿童。

ex.en: A rescue operation is under way to reach climbers trapped on the mountain.
ex.zh: 营救被困登山者的救援行动正在进行。

research.usage: [族] researcher n. 研究人员；辨析：research 指为揭示自然规律或获取新知识而进行长时间的调查研究，常译为"研究"；索引p415

ex.en: New research suggests that smell is a crucial factor in guiding elephants—and probably other herbivores—to the best food resources.
ex.zh: 新的研究表明,嗅觉是引导大象——以及可能其他草食动物——找到最佳食物资源的关键因素。

ex.en: The university carries out research into renewable energy with local industry.
ex.zh: 该大学与当地企业合作开展可再生能源研究。

ex.en: Further research is needed before the treatment can be approved for general use.
ex.zh: 这种疗法在获准普遍使用之前还需要进一步研究。

ex.en: One researcher spent two years recording the calls of wild dolphins.
ex.zh: 一名研究人员花了两年时间记录野生海豚的叫声。

ex.en: Researchers at the institute have developed a cheaper test for the virus.
ex.zh: 该研究所的研究人员开发出一种更便宜的病毒检测方法。

ex.en: Young researchers often struggle to secure funding for unfashionable subjects.
ex.zh: 年轻研究人员常常难以为冷门课题争取到资助。

resemblance.usage: 助记:resembl(e)(相似)+ance(名词后缀)→相似处；索引p415

ex.en: The resemblance between the two sisters is so strong that they are often mistaken for each other.
ex.zh: 这对姐妹长得非常相像，经常被人认错。

ex.en: The new policy bears little resemblance to the one it replaced.
ex.zh: 新政策与它所取代的旧政策几乎没有相似之处。

ex.en: There is a striking resemblance between the coastal towns of the two countries.
ex.zh: 两国沿海城镇有着惊人的相似之处。

senses: v. 看起来像；显得像；像
resemble.usage: [族] resemblance n. 相似；相似处；助记:re(again再)+semble(similar类似)→类似；v.像，与……相似；re（一再）+sem（联想成 same 一样的）+ble→一再地使他们变成一样→与……相似→像；索引p415

ex.en: The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box.
ex.zh: 该机器鼠的大小与普通老鼠一样，但（外形）却像一个简单的塑料盒。

ex.en: The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels.
ex.zh: 这个机器鼠和普通老鼠一样大，但看起来就像一个简单的、带轮子的塑料盒子。

ex.en: Modern e-cigarettes closely resemble ordinary cigarettes in shape, which worries health officials.
ex.zh: 现代电子烟的外形与普通香烟极为相似，这让卫生官员感到担忧。

resent.usage: [族] resentment n. 怨恨；愤恨；re(表示“反对”)+sent(感觉)→总是对他有反对的感觉→愤恨；怨恨；索引p415

ex.en: Many employees resent being monitored every minute, arguing that constant surveillance lowers morale rather than raising productivity.
ex.zh: 许多员工反感自己的一举一动都受到监视，认为持续的监控会打击士气，而非提高生产率。

ex.en: Local residents resent the new airport project, which they say will bring noise without creating many jobs.
ex.zh: 当地居民对新机场项目心怀不满，他们说该项目只会带来噪音，却创造不了多少就业岗位。

ex.en: Teenagers may resent parental control, yet studies show clear rules often protect rather than restrict them.
ex.zh: 青少年可能怨恨父母的管束，但研究表明，明确的规则往往是在保护而非限制他们。

resentment.usage: n.愤恨，怨恨；词根记忆: re(表强调)+sent(feel, 感受)+ment(名词后缀)→一种强烈的感受→怨恨；索引p415

ex.en: In the Internet age, it is particularly easy to see the resentment that has always been hidden within American society.
ex.zh: 在网络时代，人们能相当轻松地看到一直隐藏在美国社会中的不满情绪。

ex.en: Tax increases have caused deep resentment among middle-class voters.
ex.zh: 增税在中产阶级选民中引起了强烈的不满。

ex.en: She felt no resentment towards the colleague who took her promotion.
ex.zh: 她对夺走自己升职机会的同事毫无怨恨。

ex.en: I would like to confirm my reservation for two nights starting on Friday.
ex.zh: 我想确认从周五起两晚的预订。

ex.en: She supported the plan without reservation, despite its high cost.
ex.zh: 尽管成本高昂，她还是毫无保留地支持该计划。

ex.en: I have serious reservations about entrusting the project to an untested team.
ex.zh: 我对把项目交给一个未经考验的团队有很大保留意见。

reserve.usage: [族] reservation n. 预订；保留意见（链接P221）；re（一再）+serve（服务；提供）→一再提供→保留；预订。；词根记忆：re(向后)+serv(保持)+e→保持住，留给后面的人用→保留；索引p416

ex.en: In a world in which I don't have to work, I might feel rather different—perhaps different enough to throw himself into a hobby or a passion project with the intensity usually reserved for professional matters.
ex.zh: "身处在一个我不必工作的世界时，我可能会感觉很不一样"——或许会足以令其完全投入于一种爱好或者一个激情四溢的活动，而这种投入程度通常是从事职业活动时才会有的。

ex.en: These seats are reserved for elderly and disabled passengers.
ex.zh: 这些座位是为老年乘客和残障乘客保留的。

ex.en: The central bank holds large reserves of foreign currency.
ex.zh: 中央银行持有大量外汇储备。

reservoir.usage: reserv（联想成reserve“保留，储存”）+oir（名词后缀）→用来储存水的东西→水库；蓄水池。

ex.en: The reservoir supplies water to more than two million people.
ex.zh: 这座水库为两百多万人供水。

ex.en: Drought has left the reservoir at its lowest level in decades.
ex.zh: 干旱使水库水位降至几十年来的最低点。

ex.en: She has an enormous reservoir of patience with young children.
ex.zh: 面对幼儿，她有着极大的耐心。

senses: v. 改变……的形状(或结构);重塑,改组

ex.en: Their passports do not give them the right to reside in Britain.
ex.zh: 他们的护照没有给予他们在英国居住的权利。

residence.usage: 助记:resid(e)(居住)+ence(名词后缀)→住处；n.住宅，住所；居住；索引p416

ex.en: They had entered the country and had applied for permanent residence.
ex.zh: 他们已经入境该国，并申请了永久居住权。

ex.en: Foreign students may apply for permanent residence after working in the country for several years.
ex.zh: 外国学生在这个国家工作数年后可以申请永久居留权。

ex.en: The old building served as the official residence of the governor for nearly a century.
ex.zh: 这座古老的建筑在近一个世纪里一直用作总督的官邸。

resident.usage: [族] residence n. 居住；住所；[族] residential adj. 住宅的；索引p416

ex.en: The proposals sparked concern among local residents.
ex.zh: 这些提议引起了当地居民的担忧。

ex.en: In 2007, Indonesia started phasing in a program that gives money to its poorest residents under certain conditions, such as requiring people to keep kids in school or get regular medical care.
ex.zh: 2007年，印度尼西亚开始分阶段实施一个扶贫项目，该项目会资助那些最贫困的居民，不过需要符合一些特定条件，比如要求人们让孩子接受教育或者定期接受医疗护理。

ex.en: More than half of the city's residents now oppose the plan to build a second highway.
ex.zh: 如今该市超过一半的居民反对修建第二条高速公路的计划。

resign.usage: [族] resignation n. 辞职；辞职信；同义submit;give up,quit；sign（签字）→入职签字，再次（re）签字是离职→辞职

ex.en: She has made up her mind to resign.
ex.zh: 她已下定决心辞职。

ex.en: The minister was forced to resign over the expenses scandal.
ex.zh: 该部长因报销丑闻被迫辞职。

ex.en: He resigned from the board after only two years in the post.
ex.zh: 他上任仅两年就从董事会辞职了。

senses: n. 辞职;放弃;听任,顺从,屈从

ex.en: She handed in her resignation following the dispute over company policy.
ex.zh: 就公司政策问题发生争端后，她递交了辞呈。

senses: adj. 可迅速恢复的,有适应力的
adj. (物质)有弹性(或弹力)的,能复原的

phrases.m: adv. 有恢复力地,有弹性地

resist.usage: [族] resistance n. 抵制；抵抗力；[族] resistant adj. 抵抗的；re（相反）+sist（站）→站在对立面→反抗；withstand(抵抗)通常表示"抵挡得住",resist则不一定含有此意；re（表示“重复”，也可以表示“回去”）+sist（站）→你往回站，不跟我站在一起或再次站起来表示

ex.en: They successfully resisted pressure from their competitors to increase prices.
ex.zh: 他们成功地顶住了竞争对手提高价格的压力。

ex.en: I couldn't resist laughing at his joke.
ex.zh: 我忍不住被他的笑话逗笑了。

ex.en: Unhealthy curiosity is possible to resist, however.
ex.zh: 然而，有害身心的好奇心是可以抵制的。

resistance.usage: n.抵制；反抗；抵抗力；阻力；resist 的派生词；索引p416

ex.en: There has been a lot of resistance to this new law.
ex.zh: 这项新的法规已经遭到强烈抵制。

ex.en: The NHS trust responded to Denham's verdict with tough resistance.
ex.zh: 英国国民健康服务(NHS)基金会强烈抵制德纳姆的裁决。

ex.en: The upwash experience may save propelling energy as well as reducing resistance.
ex.zh: 在上升流中飞行可以节省推进能量，并减少阻力。

senses: adj. 抵抗的；有抵抗力的
adj. 抵抗的,有抵抗力的
resistant.usage: adj.抵制的，反抗的；有抵抗力 的；resist 的派生词；索引p416

ex.en: He is resistant to social changes.
ex.zh: 他抵制社会变革。

ex.en: California's Forest Carbon Plan endeavors to cultivate more drought-resistant trees.
ex.zh: 加利福尼亚州的"森林碳计划"致力于种植更多耐干旱的树木。

ex.en: Many bacteria are becoming resistant to common antibiotics, posing a serious threat to public health.
ex.zh: 许多细菌正对常用抗生素产生耐药性，对公共健康构成严重威胁。

senses: v. 学习新技能；教(某人)新技能

ex.en: The government remains resolute in its refusal to negotiate with the hijackers.
ex.zh: 政府坚决拒绝与劫机者谈判。

ex.en: Despite repeated setbacks, she stayed resolute in her ambition to become a surgeon.
ex.zh: 尽管屡遭挫折，她成为外科医生的决心依然坚定。

ex.en: He faced the criticism with a calm and resolute manner.
ex.zh: 他以冷静而坚决的态度面对批评。

phrases.p: make a resolution to do sth.

resolution.usage: 助记:resolut(e)(坚决的)+ion(名词后缀)→坚定；联想记忆：re(再次)+solution(解决方案)→再次想出的解决方案→决议；索引p416

ex.en: I made a New Year resolution to give up smoking.
ex.zh: 我决心在新的一年把烟戒掉。

ex.en: A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight.
ex.zh: 周二，联邦上诉法院再次发表意见，但并未提供一个人们急需的决议，而只是延长了这场争论持久战。

ex.en: The United Nations passed a resolution calling for an immediate ceasefire.
ex.zh: 联合国通过了一项呼吁立即停火的决议。

resolve.usage: [族] resolute adj. 坚决的；[族] resolution n. 决议；决心；分辨率；反义hesitate踌躇,犹豫;助记:re(再次)+solve(解决)→解决；re(重复)+solve(解决)→下决心再次解决→解决；下决心；词根记忆：re(表加强)+solv(loosen, 解开)+e→完全解开→解决

ex.en: He resolved not to tell her the truth.
ex.zh: 他决定不告诉她真相。

ex.en: Efforts to resolve the skills mismatch in Canada have appeared to be insufficient.
ex.zh: 加拿大解决技能不匹配问题的努力似乎还不够。

ex.en: Negotiators worked through the night to resolve the dispute before the strike could begin.
ex.zh: 谈判代表彻夜工作，力争在罢工开始前解决争端。

resort.usage: re-（再）+sort（出去）→一再出去（的地方）→度假胜地。搭配 resort to doing sth. 诉诸做某事；同义fall back on；re(阿姨)+sort(分类)→阿姨不懂垃圾分类只能求助于我；索引p416

ex.en: We had to resort to another loan from the bank.
ex.zh: 我们不得不求助于银行的另一笔贷款。

ex.en: The island resort attracts thousands of tourists every summer.
ex.zh: 这座岛屿度假胜地每年夏天吸引成千上万的游客。

ex.en: When talks failed, the union resorted to strike action.
ex.zh: 谈判失败后，工会诉诸罢工行动。

resource.usage: [族] resourceful adj. 机智的；资源丰富的；resource指国家或人拥有的资源财力;source指源泉;origin指来源出处,一次性；re(重复)找到金矿的源头(source)需要很多资源、财力→资源；财力；索引p416

ex.en: The website is an invaluable educational resource.
ex.zh: 该网站是一个宝贵的教育资源。

ex.en: The country is rich in natural resources such as gas and timber.
ex.zh: 这个国家拥有天然气和木材等丰富的自然资源。

ex.en: Time is the scarcest resource for most working parents.
ex.zh: 对大多数有工作的父母来说，时间是最稀缺的资源。

respect.usage: [族] respectable adj. 值得尊敬的（链接P222）；[族] respectful adj. 恭敬的；in respect to...至于,关于;without respect to/of不管;respectable adj.值得尊敬的；n.尊敬；重视，尊重；方面 v.尊敬，敬佩；遵守；n.尊敬；重视，

ex.en: This has been a difficult year in many respects.
ex.zh: 从许多方面来看，这是艰难的一年。

ex.en: Students learn more when teachers respect their opinions instead of simply correcting their mistakes.
ex.zh: 当老师尊重学生的意见而不只是纠正错误时，学生会学得更多。

ex.en: The two descriptions of the event differ greatly in this respect, which puzzled the investigators.
ex.zh: 对这个事件的两种描述在这一点上大相径庭，这让调查人员感到困惑。

senses: adj. 值得尊敬的；体面的
adj. 体面的,得体的;值得尊敬的;相当好的;不丢面子的
adj. 体面的；值得尊敬的；相当好的

ex.en: Dickens's mother supposedly came from a more respectable family.
ex.zh: 狄更斯的母亲被认为是来自一个更为体面的家庭。

ex.en: He managed a respectable second place despite the injury.
ex.zh: 尽管受伤，他还是取得了相当不错的第二名。

ex.en: She came from a respectable middle-class family of doctors and teachers.
ex.zh: 她出身于一个由医生和教师组成的体面中产家庭。

senses: adj. 恭敬的；表示尊敬的

respective.usage: [族] respectively adv. 分别地；各自地；respective（各自的）vs respectful（恭敬的）vs respectable（可敬的）；respect（方面，尊重）+ive（形容词后缀）→不插手别人的事，各自干活→分别的，各自的

ex.en: They are each recognized specialists in their respective fields.
ex.zh: 他们在各自的领域都被视为专家。

ex.en: The two ministers returned to their respective capitals for further talks.
ex.zh: 两位部长各自回国作进一步磋商。

ex.en: The winners went up to collect their respective prizes.
ex.zh: 获胜者上台领取各自的奖品。

ex.en: In February, at 3.5 percent and 5.5 percent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere.
ex.zh: 2月，加拿大和美国的失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%，处于代际低点，到处都存在劳动力短缺问题。

respond.usage: [族] response n. 回答；反应（链接P222）；[族]response n. 回答；反应；re(阿姨)+spond(联想是棒的)→这个阿姨回应很快是不是很棒→回应；词根:re(back还给)+spond(answer回答)→还给别人一个回答→作出反应；同根词根spond=to promise承诺,to an

ex.en: More than fifty people responded to the advertisement.
ex.zh: 五十多人对这个广告作出了回应。

ex.en: The company responded quickly to complaints about its product.
ex.zh: 该公司迅速回应了对其产品的投诉。

ex.en: Patients respond differently to the same treatment.
ex.zh: 患者对同一治疗的反应各不相同。

ex.en: I received an immediate response to my request.
ex.zh: 我的请求立即得到了答复。

ex.en: In response to falling sales, the retailer cut prices and expanded its online store.
ex.zh: 为应对销售下滑，这家零售商下调了价格并扩大了网上商店。

ex.en: The body's first response to infection is to raise its temperature and slow the invading virus.
ex.zh: 身体对感染的第一反应是升高体温，以减缓病毒的入侵。

responsibility.usage: [族] responsible adj. 有责任的；负责的；n.责任，职责；n.责任；n.责任，负责；另:sense of responsibility责任感；索引p416

ex.en: It's time for someone to take responsibility and get the job done.
ex.zh: 是时候有人承担责任，完成工作了。

ex.en: Parents share the responsibility for teaching children honesty, a task schools cannot complete alone.
ex.zh: 父母分担着教会孩子诚实的责任，这是学校无法单独完成的任务。

ex.en: The manager accepted full responsibility for the shipping delay and offered customers a formal apology.
ex.zh: 经理为发货延误承担全部责任，并向客户作出了正式道歉。

senses: adj. 有责任的；应负责的

phrases.m: adv. 明事理地,可信赖地

responsible.usage: adj.负责的；应担责的；作为 缘由的；respons(回答,回应)+ible(能…的)→能给出回应的人是有责任心可靠的；索引p416

ex.en: To serve as responsible stewards of the planet, we must press forward on deeper atmospheric and oceanic research.
ex.zh: 作为地球的负责任的管理者，我们必须推进对大气和海洋的更深层次的研究。

ex.en: Customers were generally responsible for paying the sales tax to the state themselves if they weren't charged it, but most didn't realize they owed it and few paid.
ex.zh: 通常来说，如果消费者未被收取销售税，他们自己有义务向州政府缴纳，但是大多数人都不曾意识到他们欠了税，也极少有人去缴纳。

ex.en: Scientists still cannot identify precisely which chemical is responsible for the mysterious illness.
ex.zh: 科学家仍无法准确查明是哪种化学物质导致了这种神秘疾病。

senses: n. 休息,睡眠;停止,静止
n. 剩余部分,其余;(the~)其余的人(或物)
adj. 不安的,坐立不安的
restless.usage: 助记:rest(休息)+less(否定后缀)→得不到休息的

senses: n. 恢复,复位,复辟;归还,交还

phrases.p: realize the high cost of data restoration
phrases.m: 意识到数据修复的成本之高

ex.en: The restoration of the cathedral took more than a decade.
ex.zh: 大教堂的修复花了十多年时间。

ex.en: The two countries agreed on the restoration of diplomatic relations.
ex.zh: 两国同意恢复外交关系。

ex.en: Funds were raised for the restoration of the medieval castle.
ex.zh: 人们为修复这座中世纪城堡筹集了资金。

phrases.p: restore sb. to a former position

restore.usage: [族] restoration n. 恢复；修复；re（回）+store（储存）→把东西放回原处→恢复；病人休息(rest)得好，才能慢慢恢复(restore)身体；真 restore public trust in financial institutions 恢复公众对金融机构的信任；索引p416

ex.en: Starting next year, any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing. The main purpose of this "clawback" rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institution.
ex.zh: 从明年开始,如果高管们的银行因不当行为受到调查,高管们所有有保证的奖金都会被延迟10年发放。这项"回拨"规则的主要目的是让银行家为不良风险承担责任,并恢复公众对金融机构的信任。

ex.en: Trust is easily destroyed and hugely expensive to restore.
ex.zh: 信任很容易被摧毁，但是恢复需要花费巨大的代价。

ex.en: Volunteers spent two years helping to restore the damaged wetlands to their natural state.
ex.zh: 志愿者们花了两年时间帮助恢复受损湿地，使其回到自然状态。

restrain.usage: curb 的近义词；inhibit 的近义词；re（回）+strain（拉紧）→往回拉→抑制。近义：suppress vt. 镇压；抑制；[族] restraint n. 抑制；约束；v.制止；克制，抑制；re（反复）+strain（拉紧）→反复拉紧→阻止，制止；索引p416

ex.en: John managed to restrain his anger.
ex.zh: 约翰努力压制住自己的怒气。

ex.en: He could barely restrain his excitement when the results confirmed years of speculation.
ex.zh: 当结果证实了多年来的猜想时，他几乎抑制不住内心的兴奋。

ex.en: The new rules are meant to restrain banks from taking risks that taxpayers would ultimately pay for.
ex.zh: 新规则旨在约束银行，防止其进行最终要由纳税人买单的风险活动。

restraint.usage: 记：re-(再)+strain(束缚)+t→一再使人感到束缚的规则→管制措施；[族]restrain vt.约束；restrained a.克制的；n.克制，抑制；限制；词根记忆：re(again,再次)+strain(draw tight,拉紧)+t→再次拉紧→限制。；索引p416

ex.en: put unnatural restraints on sb.
ex.zh: 抑制某人的天性

ex.en: Good writing often shows restraint, leaving readers to draw their own conclusions from the facts.
ex.zh: 好的写作往往有所克制，让读者自行从事实中得出结论。

ex.en: Government spending restraints introduced last year have slowed the expansion of public hospitals.
ex.zh: 去年出台的政府支出限制措施减缓了公立医院的扩张。

senses: vt. 限制，限定（数量、范围等）
vt. 限制，限定（尺寸、数量等）
restrict.usage: 族：restriction n. 限制；约束。近义：limit vt. 限制；[族] restriction n. 限制；约束；[族] restricted adj. 受限制的；re（回）+strict（拉紧）→拉回来不许越界→限制；re(重复)+strict(严格的)→一再地严格→约束，限制；索引p416

ex.en: He feels this new law will restrict the freedom of drivers.
ex.zh: 他觉得这一新法律会限制司机的自由。

ex.en: New visa rules restrict the number of foreign workers that technology companies can hire each year.
ex.zh: 新的签证规定限制了科技公司每年可雇用的外国工人数量。

ex.en: Doctors advise patients to restrict salt intake to lower the risk of high blood pressure.
ex.zh: 医生建议病人限制盐的摄入量，以降低患高血压的风险。

senses: a. 受限制的；受约束的

restriction.usage: restrict（限制）+-ion（名词后缀）→限制；restrict 的派生词；n.限制；约束；索引p416

ex.en: They have the potential to enforce restrictions such as no smoking policies.
ex.zh: 他们可能会实施一些限制措施，比如颁布禁烟政策。

ex.en: New restrictions have been placed on foreign investment.
ex.zh: 对外国投资实施了新的限制。

ex.en: The government finally lifted the restrictions on night flights.
ex.zh: 政府最终取消了夜航限制。

restrictive.usage: adj.限制性的，约束性的；索引p416

ex.en: The other reason why costs are so high is the restrictive guild-like ownership structure of the business.
ex.zh: 花费如此之高的另一个原因是该行业的所有制结构类似于协会性质，具有限制性。

ex.en: Overly restrictive immigration rules have left many hospitals unable to hire the nurses they desperately need.
ex.zh: 过于严苛的移民规定使许多医院无法聘到急需的护士。

ex.en: The restrictive terms of the contract prevent authors from publishing their work anywhere else.
ex.zh: 合同中的限制性条款阻止作者在其他任何地方发表其作品。

result.usage: 小记：as a result of 由于；result from 由…引起；2019完形例：changes in immunity that resulted from excess abdominal fat 腹部脂肪过多导致的免疫系统变化；易混辨析：result 普通用词，常用于表示事情过去之后的结果；索引p416

ex.en: These demands resulted in a very rapid expansion of the systems of higher education, beginning in the 1960s and developing very rapidly (though unevenly) during the 1970s and 1980s.
ex.zh: 这些需求导致了高等教育体系的迅速扩张，它（该体系）始于20世纪60年代，在20世纪70年代和80年代迅速发展（尽管并不平衡）。

ex.en: The road accident resulted from a combination of bad weather and driver fatigue.
ex.zh: 这起交通事故是恶劣天气和司机疲劳共同造成的。

ex.en: Students will receive their exam results by post at the end of August.
ex.zh: 学生将在八月底通过邮寄收到考试成绩。

senses: adj. 作为结果而发生的,必然发生的

resume.usage: [族] resumption n. 恢复；重新开始；同义continue；re（重新）+sum（总计，总和）+e→重新计算总和→重新开始

ex.en: She resumed her career after an interval of six years.
ex.zh: 时隔六年之后她又开始了自己的职业生涯。

ex.en: Talks are expected to resume once both sides have consulted their governments.
ex.zh: 预计双方与各自政府磋商后将恢复会谈。

ex.en: Passengers were allowed to resume their journey after the track had been repaired.
ex.zh: 铁轨修复后，乘客们得以继续旅程。

retail.usage: [反] wholesale n. 批发；[反]wholesale n. 批发；[族]retailer n. 零售商；助记:与whole sale(批发)一起记;派生retailer n.零售商；re（再）+tail（切）→已经切过了，再切→零售

ex.en: Retail trade groups praised the ruling, saying it levels the playing field for local and online businesses.
ex.zh: 零售贸易团体赞扬了这项裁决，称其为地方商家和在线商家创造了公平的竞争环境。

ex.en: The retail sector has been hit hard by the shift to online shopping.
ex.zh: 零售业受到向网上购物转变的严重冲击。

ex.en: The book retails at about twenty dollars.
ex.zh: 这本书的零售价约为二十美元。

retain.usage: re-（回）+tain（拿住）→拿回来→保留。近义：keep vt. 保持；[近] keep vt. 保持；保留；re（回）+tain（拿）→拿回来→保留；助记:re(back回来)+tain(hold拿)→拿回来→保留;同义keep,preserve,hold,maintain;反义abandon v.抛弃,放弃；v

ex.en: The house retains much of its original charm.
ex.zh: 这所房子保留了许多原有的魅力。

ex.en: Their engineers were retained.
ex.zh: 他们的工程师留了下来。

ex.en: Students retain information far better when they review it at intervals rather than cramming all at once.
ex.zh: 学生分阶段复习时对信息的记忆远远好于一次性突击灌输。

retire.usage: [族] retirement n. 退休；[族] retired adj. 退休的；助记:re(back返回)+tire(劳累)→太劳累了就回家→退休;派生retiree n.退休人员;retirement n.退休,退职;引退；re(阿姨)+tire(疲劳，疲倦)→阿姨累了所以不工作了→退休；索引p416

ex.en: Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs.
ex.zh: 同时，它还背负着一千两百多亿美元的无资金准备债务，主要用于员工医保和退休金。

ex.en: She retired from teaching at sixty after thirty-five years in the classroom.
ex.zh: 她执教三十五年后，六十岁从教学岗位上退休。

ex.en: The injured player was forced to retire from the match.
ex.zh: 那名受伤的球员被迫退出了比赛。

ex.en: Many retirees move to coastal towns where the cost of living is lower.
ex.zh: 许多退休人员搬到生活成本较低的沿海城镇。

ex.en: The pension scheme guarantees each retiree a fixed monthly income.
ex.zh: 该养老金计划保证每位退休人员有固定的月收入。

ex.en: Retirees are being recruited to mentor students who lack role models.
ex.zh: 退休人员正被招募来指导缺乏榜样的学生。

ex.en: After his retirement, he devoted himself to gardening and voluntary work.
ex.zh: 退休后，他全身心投入园艺和志愿工作。

ex.en: The number of Americans staying in work beyond retirement age has risen sharply.
ex.zh: 超过退休年龄仍在工作的美国人数量急剧上升。

ex.en: She announced her retirement from international tennis at the age of thirty.
ex.zh: 她三十岁时宣布从国际网坛退役。

retort.usage: 助记:re(back回来)+tort(twist扭曲)→扭转过来→反驳；re（回）+tort（扭）→往回扭→反驳。

ex.en: Sam retorted that it was my fault as much as his.
ex.zh: 萨姆反驳说我和他同样有错。

ex.en: “That is none of your business,” she retorted angrily.
ex.zh: “那不关你的事，”她愤怒地回嘴道。

ex.en: He made a sharp retort, and the discussion ended in silence.
ex.zh: 他尖刻地反驳了一句，讨论便在沉默中结束。

retreat.usage: [近] withdraw vi. 撤退；re（回）+treat（走）→往回走→撤退；re(往回，向后)+treat(=tract回拉)→往回拉→撤退，后退；索引p416

ex.en: The retreat from predominance proved painful.
ex.zh: 从优势地位退出被证明是痛苦的。

ex.en: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work—be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day.
ex.zh: 想要精通深度工作技能有很多种方法——为了投入一项特定的任务而长时间闭关；养成每天例行公事；或者是采用"新闻工作者"的办法，抓住一天中能够深度工作的时刻。

ex.en: The army was forced to retreat across the frozen river.
ex.zh: 军队被迫撤退，渡过冰封的河流。

retribution.usage: re（回来）+tribut（给）+ion（名词后缀）→给回来→惩罚，报应。

ex.en: Evil actions will bring retribution.
ex.zh: 恶行会有恶报。

senses: v. 重新得到,恢复,补偿;更正;拯救;想起(忘记的事情)

phrases.m: 重新获得某物,取回某物

retrieve.usage: 助记:re(again再)+trieve(find找到)→重新得到;派生retrievable adj.可检索的;retrieval n.重获,取回,挽回

retrospect.usage: 助记:retro(backward向后)+spect(look看)→回顾;派生retrospection n.回顾;追溯;retrospective adj.回顾的；索引p416

reveal.usage: [族] revelation n. 揭露；披露；[族] revelation n. 揭露；暴露；族：revelation n. 揭露；披露。近义：disclose v. 揭露，透露；disclose 的近义词；[族] revelation n. 揭露；披露；[近] disclose vt. 揭露；reveal 反义词

ex.en: The study reveals the link between diet and health.
ex.zh: 这项研究揭示了饮食与健康之间的联系。

ex.en: The 1990 Census revealed that "a majority of immigrants from each of the fifteen most common countries of origin spoke English 'well' or 'very well' after ten years of residence".
ex.zh: 1990年的人口普查显示，"来自最常见的15个移民输出国的移民中，大多数人在美国居住了十年后英语都讲得'不错'或'非常好'"。

ex.en: Documents leaked to the press reveal serious flaws in the safety inspection system.
ex.zh: 泄露给媒体的文件揭露了安全检查系统中的严重缺陷。

senses: n. 被暴露的真相,被曝光的秘密(c)
n. 被透露的事实；揭露
revelation.usage: reveal 的派生词；n.被揭示的真相、；揭露；（上 帝的）启示；索引p416

ex.en: The revelation of the secret payments shocked the whole industry.
ex.zh: 这笔秘密款项的披露震惊了整个行业。

ex.en: Her memoirs contain several startling revelations about the royal family.
ex.zh: 她的回忆录包含若干关于王室的惊人内幕。

ex.en: The report was a revelation to investors who had trusted the firm's accounts.
ex.zh: 这份报告让一直信任该公司账目的投资者大为震惊。

revenge.usage: be revenged on sb.向某人复仇;典型考题get his__on选A.revenge(wrath暴怒;indignation愤怒;punishment惩罚)

senses: n. 税收，财政收入；收益
n. （政府的）税收，财政收入；（企业）收益
revenue.usage: [近] income n. 收入；re（回）+ven（来）+ue→回来的东西→收入。；revenue 指总收入/财政收入；income 个人收入。；易混：revenue指公司/机构收入，还可专指政府税收；income指工作收入或投资收益。；索引p416

ex.en: The company's annual revenues rose by 30%.
ex.zh: 公司的年收入增加了30%。

ex.en: The state's tax revenue increased last year.
ex.zh: 去年该州的税收收入增加了。

ex.en: Advertising is the main source of revenue for the website.
ex.zh: 广告是该网站的主要收入来源。

ex.en: The Supreme Court's opinion Thursday overruled a pair of decades-old decisions that states said cost them billions of dollars in lost revenue annually.
ex.zh: 最高法院周四做出的裁决推翻了两项实行了数十年之久的决策，各州声称，这两项决策使得他们每年损失数十亿美元的财政收入。

reverse.usage: 族：reversal n. 倒转；推翻。近义：overturn vt. 推翻；[族] reversible adj. 可逆的；[族] reversal n. 逆转；撤销；re（回去）+verse（转）→往回转→逆转；使反转；相反的；词根记忆：re(back, 回)+vers(turn, 转)+e→转回来→彻底转变；索引

ex.en: The networked computer offers the first chance in 50 years to reverse the flow.
ex.zh: 50年来,电脑网络给我们提供了首次可扭转这一模式的机会。

ex.en: They suffered a serious political reverse.
ex.zh: 他们在政治上遭遇严重挫折。

ex.en: Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food.
ex.zh: 一些人将英国脱欧视为可以扭转近期英国进口食品趋势的一个机会。

revert.usage: re（回）+vert（转）→转回去→恢复。近义：return vi. 返回

review.usage: [族] reviewer n. 评论者；审稿人；索引p416

ex.en: Yet a considerable number of the most significant collections of criticism published in the 20th century consisted in large part of newspaper reviews.
ex.zh: 然而，在20世纪出版的相当数量最有影响的评论文集中，报刊上的评论占了很大一部分。

ex.en: The committee will review the safety procedures following the accident.
ex.zh: 事故发生后，委员会将审查安全程序。

ex.en: Her first novel received favourable reviews in almost every newspaper.
ex.zh: 她的首部小说几乎在每家报纸都获得了好评。

ex.en: The reviewer praised the film's photography but criticised its weak plot.
ex.zh: 评论家称赞了这部电影的摄影，但批评其情节薄弱。

ex.en: Reviewers were asked to evaluate the paper anonymously.
ex.zh: 审稿人被要求匿名评审这篇论文。

ex.en: One reviewer described the novel as the finest of its decade.
ex.zh: 一位评论家称这部小说是十年来最优秀的作品。

revise.usage: [族] revision n. 修改；修订；复习；[族]revision n. 修订；复习；同义①amend②correct,improve；v.改变；修改，修订；复习；v.改变，修正；修改，修订； 复习；re(又，再)+vis(看)+e→重复地看→修改；复习；索引p416

ex.en: The government may need to revise its policy in the light of this report.
ex.zh: 政府可能需要根据这份报告改变其政策。

ex.en: The editors asked her to revise the article so that its conclusions followed clearly from the evidence.
ex.zh: 编辑请她修改这篇文章，使其结论能清晰地依据证据得出。

ex.en: Faced with new fossil evidence, scientists had to revise their assumptions about how birds evolved.
ex.zh: 面对新的化石证据，科学家不得不修正有关鸟类演化的假设。

senses: n. 修订,校订,修正;复习,温习
revision.usage: 词根记忆：re(again, 重新)+vis(see, 看)+e→再看一遍→复习；索引p416

ex.en: The textbook is currently under revision, and a new edition will appear next year.
ex.zh: 该教科书正在修订中，新版本将于明年出版。

ex.en: He failed the exam in June but passed after a summer of intensive revision.
ex.zh: 他六月考试不及格，但经过一个暑假的集中复习后通过了。

ex.en: The policy needs a thorough revision to reflect changes in the labour market.
ex.zh: 这项政策需要全面修订，以反映劳动力市场的变化。

senses: v. 使新生,使恢复元气,使有新的活力
n. 苏醒,复活,再生,恢复
revival.usage: n.复兴，复苏；再流行；重新 上演；索引p416

ex.en: Cheap air travel has led to a revival of interest in foreign holidays.
ex.zh: 廉价航空旅行使人们对出国度假的兴趣复苏。

ex.en: There are signs of an economic revival in the depressed northern towns.
ex.zh: 有迹象表明，萧条的北方城镇正出现经济复苏。

ex.en: The play's revival on Broadway drew enthusiastic reviews.
ex.zh: 该剧在百老汇的重演获得了热烈的好评。

senses: v. 复活，苏醒；重新使用
revive.usage: 同义regenerate,restore,refresh,renew；v.(使)复原，(使)复苏；使复 兴；re（再，又）+vive（活）→又活一遍→复活，苏醒。；词根记忆：re(again, 再次)+vive(live, 存在)→再次存在→恢复；索引p416

ex.en: And, unless banks carry toxic assets at prices that attract buyers, reviving the banking system will be difficult.
ex.zh: 而且，如果银行不以能够吸引买家的价格出售不良资产，银行系统的复苏将会非常困难。

ex.en: The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier.
ex.zh: 应对自动化的挑战凸显出美国需要重振其日渐衰退的经济活力：必须要让开创新公司变得更容易。

ex.en: The government is trying to revive the economy through tax cuts.
ex.zh: 政府正试图通过减税来振兴经济。

revolt.usage: 助记:re(against反)+volt(roll转)→反转→反抗,叛乱;辨析:revolt类似revolution,指大规模有组织且用暴力的反抗;rebel,rebellion仅指局部的反抗行为

revolution.usage: n.变革；革命；旋转；旋转一 周；索引p416

ex.en: The Industrial Revolution transformed Britain within a few generations.
ex.zh: 工业革命在几代人之内改变了英国。

ex.en: Digital technology has brought about a revolution in publishing.
ex.zh: 数字技术给出版业带来了一场革命。

ex.en: The earth makes one revolution around the sun every year.
ex.zh: 地球每年绕太阳旋转一周。

revolutionary.usage: 助记:revolution(革命)+ary(名词后缀表示人)→革命者；索引p416

ex.en: The new treatment is regarded as revolutionary in the fight against cancer.
ex.zh: 这种新疗法被视为抗癌斗争中的革命性突破。

ex.en: Revolutionary ideas about education spread quickly among young teachers.
ex.zh: 关于教育的革新思想在年轻教师中迅速传播。

ex.en: The revolutionaries seized the palace and announced a new government.
ex.zh: 革命者占领了宫殿并宣布成立新政府。

revolve.usage: rotate 的近义词；助记:re(again再)+volve(roll卷)→旋转；v.旋转；围绕；以……为中心；adj.旋转的；re（表示重复）+volv（旋转）+e→重复地旋转→旋转；环绕；索引p416

ex.en: In the first year or so of Web business, most of the action has revolved around efforts to tap the consumer market.
ex.zh: 在网络交易的第一年左右，大部分活动都是围绕着努力开发消费者市场而进行的。

ex.en: Much of the debate revolves around whether artificial intelligence will create more jobs than it destroys.
ex.zh: 争论的焦点大多围绕人工智能创造的就业岗位是否会多于其摧毁的数量。

ex.en: The Earth revolves around the Sun once a year, an idea that once provoked fierce opposition.
ex.zh: 地球每年绕太阳一周，这一观念曾激起激烈的反对。

reward.usage: [族] rewarding adj. 有益的；值得做的；reward（报答）vs award（颁发；奖项）；award指正式或官方颁布授予,可指法庭裁决,后接双宾语;reward指做好事得回报,不接双宾语,以何为报酬须加with；n.奖励，回报；报偿，报 应 v.酬谢，奖赏；奖励；re(再)+ward(联想成word“

ex.en: Scientists need journals in which to publish their research, so they will supply the articles without monetary reward.
ex.zh: 科学家需要一些期刊来发表他们的研究成果，因此他们会无偿提供文章。

ex.en: There is an intrinsic reward in solving a difficult problem, quite apart from any prize.
ex.zh: 解出一道难题本身就有内在的回报，与任何奖品无关。

ex.en: Companies that reward loyalty with real career opportunities tend to keep their best employees.
ex.zh: 以真正的职业发展机会回报员工忠诚的公司往往能留住最优秀的人才。

senses: adj. 有益的；值得做的；令人满意的
n. [U] 华而不实的言语；花言巧语
n. 华而不实的言语,花言巧语
rhetoric.usage: [族] rhetorical a. 辞藻华丽的 [族] rhetorically ad. 善用言辞地；同义:eloquence,oratory

senses: n. [U, C] 规律；规则变化
rhythm.usage: [族] rhythmic adj. 有节奏的；本身为词根，意为“节奏”；[族] rhythmic a. 有节奏的；rhythmically ad. 有节奏地

rib.usage: 助记:rid(去掉)布料上的rib(罗纹)

senses: n. 缎带,丝带,带,带状物
a. 富有的；富饶的；丰富多彩的；油腻的；肥沃的

phrases.m: 饱和的、竞争激烈的市场

rich.usage: [族] enrich vt. 使富裕；充实（链接P348）；索引p416

ex.en: The region is rich in minerals, which attracts mining companies from abroad.
ex.zh: 该地区矿产丰富，吸引了国外的矿业公司。

ex.en: The gap between rich and poor cities has widened over the past decade.
ex.zh: 过去十年，富裕城市与贫困城市之间的差距扩大了。

ex.en: The soil in the valley is remarkably rich, supporting two harvests a year.
ex.zh: 山谷里的土壤非常肥沃，一年可收获两次。

senses: ad. 富丽堂皇地；完全地；大方地

ex.en: The city has spent millions trying to rid itself of traffic congestion.
ex.zh: 这座城市已花费数百万美元试图摆脱交通拥堵。

ex.en: It is difficult to get rid of the habit of checking the phone every few minutes.
ex.zh: 很难改掉每隔几分钟就看一次手机的习惯。

ex.en: Farmers were urged to rid their fields of the invasive weed.
ex.zh: 农民们被敦促清除田里的入侵杂草。

senses: adj. 可笑的,荒唐的,荒谬的
ridiculous.usage: [族] ridicule vt.&n. 嘲笑；奚落；助记:ridicule(讥笑)+ous(形容词后缀)→可笑的

ex.en: I look ridiculous in this hat.
ex.zh: 我戴这顶帽子看上去很可笑。

ex.en: It would be ridiculous to claim that any single policy can end unemployment.
ex.zh: 声称任何单一政策都能消除失业是荒谬的。

ex.en: The price they are asking for the old house is absolutely ridiculous.
ex.zh: 他们对那栋老房子的要价实在离谱。

senses: a. 正确的；恰当的；右边的

phrases.p: have the right to do sth.

right.usage: [族] rightly adv. 正确地；[族] righteous adj. 正当的

senses: adj. 公正的,正直的,正当的
ad. 恰当地；正确地；精确地；理由充分地
a. 严格死板的，僵化的
a. 固执的；一成不变的
rigid.usage: [族]rigidly 严格地；[近]inflexible 顽固的；僵化的；反义flexible adj.柔韧的;灵活的；adj.严格死板的，僵化的；顽固 的；索引p416

ex.en: Today, we are much more rigid about immigrants.
ex.zh: 今天，我们对移民的态度要严格得多。

ex.en: Rigid school schedules leave little room for the creativity that employers increasingly demand.
ex.zh: 僵化的学校课程安排几乎没有为雇主日益看重的创造力留出空间。

senses: adj. 严格（严密）的；严厉的
adj. 严格的，严厉的；谨慎的；细致的；彻底的
rigorous.usage: 派生rigorousness n.严厉;严峻；发音类似“若哥惹事”→哥哥惹事妈妈会严厉处罚→严厉的。；索引p416

ex.en: Schooling and rigorous book learning put unnatural restraints on children.
ex.zh: 学校教育和严格的课本学习对孩子们施加了不自然的限制。

ex.en: All new drugs must pass rigorous safety testing.
ex.zh: 所有新药都必须通过严格的安全测试。

ex.en: The training involves a rigorous schedule of physical exercise.
ex.zh: 这项训练包括严格紧凑的体育锻炼安排。

rim.usage: 辨析:rim指曲线形或圆形的边(如碗边);edge指明显的终端线,常含锋利之意

senses: vi. 参加暴乱；聚众闹事
riot.usage: [族] rioter n. 暴徒；暴乱者；派生riotous adj.无秩序的,混乱的;riotously adv.极端地

senses: adj. 成熟的,时机成熟的
n. [C] （数量或水平的）增加；加薪
rise.usage: [辨] rise-rose-risen 不及物；[近] arise vi. 产生（链接P346）；辨析：不及物动词，过去式rose，过去分词risen，含义为“增加，提高，上升”；索引p416

ex.en: Everybody loves a fat pay rise.
ex.zh: 人人都喜欢大幅加薪。

ex.en: Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy.
ex.zh: 由于零工经济的兴起，“Z一代”正在寻求更多的确定性和稳定性。

ex.en: The rise in unemployment has put pressure on public finances.
ex.zh: 失业率上升给公共财政带来了压力。

risk.usage: [族] risky adj. 危险的；冒险的；另：take a risk冒险；reduce the risk of降低…的风险；at risk处境危险、受到威胁；索引p416

ex.en: When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation's diversity of gifts.
ex.zh: 当教育变得一刀切的时候，就会存在忽视一个国家人才多样化的风险。

ex.en: Smokers face a much higher risk of heart disease than non-smokers.
ex.zh: 吸烟者患心脏病的风险远高于不吸烟者。

ex.en: The company risked everything on a single untested product.
ex.zh: 公司把一切押在一个未经检验的产品上。

senses: n. 程序；（尤指）宗教仪式
adj. 典礼的,(宗教)仪式的;通常的,习惯的
n. 典礼,(宗教)仪式,礼节
ritual.usage: 本身为词根，意为“宗教仪式”。近义：ceremony n. 仪式。；索引p416

ex.en: Drinking tea in the afternoon is a daily ritual in many British homes.
ex.zh: 下午喝茶是许多英国家庭的日常惯例。

ex.en: The tribe performed an ancient ritual before the harvest.
ex.zh: 这个部落在收获前举行古老的仪式。

ex.en: Their evening walk became a comforting ritual for the old couple.
ex.zh: 傍晚散步成了这对老夫妇令人慰藉的固定习惯。

senses: a. 仪式的；例行公事的

phrases.m: 为……之竞争者,在……方面同样好

rival.usage: [近] competitor n. 竞争者；n.竞争对手，敌手；对手(rival)马上就要到达(arrival)比赛现场；索引p416

ex.en: Court, school, organizations of amateurs, and the traveling actors were all rivals in supplying a widespread desire for dramatic entertainment.
ex.zh: 宫廷、学校、业余组织和巡演艺人都在竞相满足人们对戏剧娱乐的普遍需求。

ex.en: No rival company has yet matched the quality of its cameras at such a low price.
ex.zh: 迄今还没有竞争对手能在如此低的价格下提供同等品质的相机。

ex.en: The two universities have long been rivals for research funding and the brightest students.
ex.zh: 这两所大学长期以来一直在科研经费和最优秀生源上相互竞争。

ex.en: The city grew wealthy because it controlled trade along the river.
ex.zh: 这座城市因控制沿河贸易而变得富裕。

ex.en: Industrial waste was discharged directly into the river for decades.
ex.zh: 几十年来，工业废水被直接排入河中。

ex.en: The village lies on the northern bank of the river.
ex.zh: 这个村庄坐落在河的北岸。

road.usage: [近] path n. 小路；路径；[近] route n. 路线

rob.usage: 辨析:rob对象是人,steal对象是物;rob用rob sb. of sth.,steal用steal sth. from sb.

robot.usage: [族] robotics n. 机器人学；[族] robotic adj. 机器人的

senses: n. (用作单数)机器人学,机器人技术
adj. 强大的；强健的；坚决的；粗野的
robust.usage: 派生robustly adv.有活力地;robustness n.强健、粗野；adj.强健的；稳固的；结实的；索引p416

ex.en: The economy remains robust despite uncertainty in global markets.
ex.zh: 尽管全球市场存在不确定性，经济依然强劲。

ex.en: The conclusions rest on robust evidence collected over twenty years.
ex.zh: 这些结论基于二十年间收集的可靠证据。

ex.en: Children need robust challenge as well as praise if they are to develop confidence.
ex.zh: 孩子们既需要表扬，也需要有力的挑战，才能培养自信。

rock.usage: [族] rocky adj. 岩石的；困难的；辨析:rock剧烈摇动;swing上端固定下端摇;sway下端固定上端摇

phrases.p: have a rod in pickle for someone
make a rod for one's own back

senses: adj. 离群的;行为失常的;暴戾的
vt.&vi. （使）翻滚，滚动；（使）翻身，翻转
adj. 不切实际的,好幻想的
romantic.usage: [族] romance n. 浪漫史；传奇；助记:音"罗曼蒂克"

root.usage: n.根，根茎;根源，起因 v.扎根于；根源在于

ex.en: The tree's roots were damaged when the road was widened.
ex.zh: 道路拓宽时，这棵树的根被损坏了。

ex.en: Doctors say the root of the problem lies in patients' lifestyles, not in the health system.
ex.zh: 医生说问题的根源在于病人的生活方式，而不在于医疗体系。

ex.en: Unemployment is at the root of much of the social unrest in the region.
ex.zh: 失业是该地区许多社会动荡的根源。

senses: adj. 粉红色的,红润的;美好的,乐观的

ex.en: The wood must not get damp as rot can quickly result.
ex.zh: 木头不能受潮，否则很快就会烂掉。

ex.en: Fallen apples were left to rot in the orchard.
ex.zh: 掉落的苹果被留在果园里烂掉了。

ex.en: Critics argued that the failure of the schools was a symptom of deeper social rot.
ex.zh: 批评者认为，学校的失败是更深层社会腐朽的征兆。

rotate.usage: 族：rotation n. 旋转；轮作。近义：revolve v. 旋转；[记] rot（转）+-ate（动词后缀）。[族] rotation n. 旋转；转动。[近] spin（使）快速旋转；辨析：rotate 以自身内部轴为中心旋转；revolve 以他物为轴或点作为中心旋转；roll 指一个物体在另一物体表面上滚

ex.en: The EU presidency rotates among the members.
ex.zh: 欧盟主席一职由其成员国轮流担任。

ex.en: The restaurant's floor rotates slowly, giving diners a view of the whole city.
ex.zh: 餐厅的地板缓缓旋转，让用餐者可以饱览全城景色。

ex.en: Doctors rotate between different departments during their first year of training.
ex.zh: 医生在培训的第一年在不同科室轮转。

senses: n. 旋转，转动；轮换；交替；换班
n. (有圆顶的)圆形建筑;圆形大厅

phrases.m: (对某人来说)不愉快的,不幸的

rough.usage: [反] smooth adj. 光滑的；[族] roughly adv. 大约；粗略地；派生 roughly adv. 粗暴地,差不多；索引p416

ex.en: There were about 20 people there, at a rough guess.
ex.zh: 那里约计有20人。

ex.en: He made a rough calculation and concluded that the repairs would cost more than the car was worth.
ex.zh: 他粗略估算了一下，得出结论：修理费将超过这辆车的价值。

ex.en: The path across the mountains is rough and narrow, so hikers are advised to wear strong boots.
ex.zh: 穿越山区的路径崎岖狭窄，因此建议徒步者穿上结实的靴子。

senses: adv. 大约；粗暴地；粗糙地
roughly.usage: adv.粗略地，大约；粗暴地；索引p416

ex.en: Fossil fuels—coal, oil, gas—still generate roughly 85 percent of the world's energy supply.
ex.zh: 化石燃料——煤炭、石油、天然气——仍然占世界能源供应的85%左右。

ex.en: The two groups contain roughly the same number of students.
ex.zh: 这两组包含的学生人数大致相同。

ex.en: He pushed the door roughly and it came off its hinges.
ex.zh: 他粗鲁地推门，门从铰链上脱落了。

senses: adj. 绕道的,绕圈子的,不直接的
n. 绕行路线,环行交叉,环形交通枢纽
roundabout.usage: n.环岛；旋转圆台 adj.绕路的，迂回的

phrases.m: 激起(某人的)情绪或行动

route.usage: [辨] 美 [raʊt] [raʊt]，英 [ruːt]；route常指较远的路线,可能包括若干段路程;course常指溪流、天体等自然形成的轨道;way指各种道路,用途最广

ex.en: The airline has opened a new route between London and Chengdu.
ex.zh: 这家航空公司开通了伦敦与成都之间的一条新航线。

ex.en: Engineers chose the safest route for the new railway through the mountains.
ex.zh: 工程师为穿越山区的新铁路选择了最安全的路线。

ex.en: She took the unusual route of publishing her research online for free.
ex.zh: 她走了不同寻常的路，将研究成果在网上免费发表。

routine.usage: [族] routinely adv. 例行地；常规地；n.常规，惯例 adj.常规的，例行的；平淡乏味 的；发音类似"路听"→很多老板行程满，在路上听秘书汇报日常工作→例行程；串词记忆：惯例(routine)就是按照常规的路线(route)走；索引p416

ex.en: Make exercise a part of your daily routine.
ex.zh: 让锻炼成为你日常生活的一部分。

ex.en: It makes it hard to disengage, and leads to a lot of bleed-over into the family routine.
ex.zh: 它（指数字产品）让人欲罢不能，也给家庭日常带来了严重影响。

ex.en: Checking the equipment before every flight is a routine that pilots are never allowed to skip.
ex.zh: 每次飞行前检查设备是飞行员绝不允许省略的例行程序。

senses: adv. 例行地；常规地；通常
ad. 例行地；常规地；通常地；惯常地
routinely.usage: adv.例行公事地；惯常地；索引p416

ex.en: Patients are now routinely asked about their mental health during check-ups.
ex.zh: 如今，患者在体检时都会被例行询问心理健康状况。

ex.en: The agency routinely inspects food factories twice a year.
ex.zh: 该机构每年对食品厂进行两次例行检查。

ex.en: Complaints about noise were routinely ignored by the former management.
ex.zh: 前管理层对噪音投诉一贯置之不理。

row.usage: have(或get into)a row with sb. 与某人争吵

senses: adj. 王室的，皇家的；盛大的
royal.usage: [记]来自 roy（=reg 统治）+ -al（……的）→统治的→王室的；[族] royalty n. 王室成员；[族] royalty n. 王室成员；版税；loyal adj. 忠诚的（注意区分）；adj.国王的，王室的；adj.国王的，王室的；皇家的； 盛大的；对王室（royal）要忠诚（loyal）。

ex.en: The royal family will attend the opening of the new hospital.
ex.zh: 王室成员将出席新医院的落成典礼。

ex.en: The ship received a royal welcome when it returned home.
ex.zh: 这艘船返航时受到了盛大的欢迎。

ex.en: The park was created under a royal decree two centuries ago.

senses: a. 粗鲁的；无礼的；粗野的；粗糙的；猛烈的

phrases.p: It's rude of sb. to do sth.

rude.usage: [族] rudeness n. 无礼；粗鲁；派生 rudely adv. 无礼地,粗暴地；rudeness n. 无礼,粗暴

ruin.usage: [近] destroy vt. 破坏；damage vt. 损坏；辨析：ruin 与 destroy 都有彻底毁坏或破坏之意,常可互换；destroy 强调用武力或十分彻底地破坏,使人难以修复；派生 ruination n. 毁坏(的起因),祸根；ruinous adj. 带来巨大损失的；n.毁坏；破产 v.毁坏，破坏

ex.en: We do not ruin urban conservation areas.
ex.zh: 我们不会破坏城市保护区。

ex.en: A single mistake could ruin the company's reputation.
ex.zh: 一个失误就可能毁掉公司的声誉。
